The Estate

A 1916 Neo-Georgian estate, restored to the studs.

Built for Walter Hines Page, United States Ambassador to the Court of St James's, and held by a line of stewards for more than a century. Rare handmade red brick laid in Flemish bond above a classic water table. Restored 1999 to 2001: plumbing, electrical, and climate systems replaced, custom Marvin windows throughout, Georgian millwork integrated room by room.

The 1916 fabric remains: seven carved mantels, restored original oak floors, leaded sidelights, arched fanlights above six panel solid wood doors, original brass key plates. A first floor primary wing, a library with floor to ceiling shelving, a sitting room with Delft tile fireplace and spiral staircase, and a kitchen of reclaimed heart pine and black granite.

Outside: a saltwater pool within a brick walled garden, a rear brick terrace, two lighted regulation tennis courts ready for new surfaces, mature longleaf pines, a camellia garden, and the Wee Cottage playhouse. The last remaining parcel of the original Garran Hill estate.
